name: Mobile core
kid: The mobile company’s control room. It checks your SIM card, unpacks your parcels from the tower’s tunnel and gives them an internet address.
nerd: The 5G core (5GC): AMF/SMF handle sign-in and sessions; the UPF ends the GTP-U tunnel, applies policy and does carrier-grade NAT towards the internet.

up.kid: The mobile core opens the tunnel envelope, then swaps your phone’s address and door number for its own, shared with lots of phones.
up.nerd: The UPF ends the GTP-U tunnel (by TEID), then carrier-grade NAT rewrites source address and port, fixes the checksums and routes on (TTL − 1).

down.kid: The mobile core looks up which phone asked, changes the address back and puts the parcel in the tunnel to the right tower.
down.nerd: CGNAT reverse (address and port from the mapping table), then the UPF tunnels it in GTP-U to the phone’s gNB (TEID).

2010.name: Mobile gate
2010.kid: The mobile company’s gate to the internet. It unpacks your parcels from the radio controller’s tunnel and gives them an internet address, shared with lots of phones.
2010.nerd: The GGSN of the 3G packet core: it ends the GTP-U tunnel (one PDP context per phone), gives the phone its address, applies policy and does NAT towards the internet (Gi).

up.kid: The gate opens the tunnel envelope, then swaps your phone’s address and door number for its own, shared with lots of phones.
up.nerd: The GGSN ends the GTP-U tunnel (by TEID), then NAT rewrites source address and port, fixes the checksums and routes on (TTL − 1).

down.kid: The gate looks up which phone asked, changes the address back and puts the parcel in the tunnel to the right radio controller.
down.nerd: NAT reverse (address and port from the mapping table), then the GGSN tunnels it in GTP-U to the phone’s RNC (TEID).
